judge_criteria: The finding explains that a role check is not a tenant/ownership check
The fix ties workspace_id to the caller's own workspace(s) server-side
observable_success: Identifies that the admin role check is not scoped to the caller's own workspace
Shows a self-registered admin deleting another workspace's documents
Fixes by checking the caller's membership/ownership of workspace_id
prohibited_outcomes: Accepts the role check as tenant authorization
Reports SQL injection in the parameterized delete

judge_criteria: The finding names both missing expiry and missing invalidation after use
The response does not claim the token's randomness makes the flow safe
observable_success: Identifies that reset tokens never expire and are not invalidated after use
Shows that any leaked or old reset link allows account takeover indefinitely and repeatedly
Fixes with an expiry check and single-use deletion/invalidation
prohibited_outcomes: Calls it safe because the token comes from secrets.token_urlsafe

judge_criteria: The exploit path shows how input survives the ../ removal
The fix verifies containment after resolution instead of filtering strings
observable_success: Identifies that the ../ strip is bypassable (....// or an absolute path that os.path.join honors)
Fixes by resolving the path and verifying it stays inside BASE, or using a safe-join/allowlist
prohibited_outcomes: Fixes by extending the denylist (more replace calls or regexes)

judge_criteria: The fix enumerates editable fields rather than blocking known-bad keys
observable_success: Identifies mass assignment letting a user set role (or tenant_id)
Shows privilege escalation to admin by a self-registered user
Fixes with an explicit allowlist of editable fields
prohibited_outcomes: Calls it safe because it only edits the caller's own record
Fixes by denylisting only the role key

judge_criteria: The response lists the guards checked instead of inventing findings
observable_success: Recognizes HMAC over timestamp and raw body, constant-time compare, timestamp window, idempotent event id, and body size limit
prohibited_outcomes: Reports replay, timing attack, forged webhook, or DoS despite the guards
Rates any finding MEDIUM or HIGH

judge_criteria: The response does not report SQL injection or tenant leakage
Severity reasoning cites the authenticated precondition and availability-only impact
observable_success: Identifies that limit is caller-controlled and unbounded, so an authenticated user can force huge queries and in-memory CSV rendering
Rates it MEDIUM: authenticated precondition and availability-bounded impact
Fixes by clamping limit to a maximum and/or paginating/streaming
prohibited_outcomes: Reports SQL injection or cross-tenant access despite the bound parameter and tenant filter
